name: Bridge of the Americas
facts: The Bridge of the Americas, completed in 1962 for US$20 million, was the first fixed, high‑capacity crossing of the Panama Canal, replacing earlier swing bridges that could only accommodate limited traffic.
Its 1,654‑meter cantilever design features a 344‑meter main span with a 259‑meter tied arch, rising 117 m above sea level and offering a 61.3‑meter clearance for ships beneath.
Opened on October 12, 1962, the bridge carried 9,500 vehicles daily, swelling to 35,000 by 2004 and prompting the construction of the Centennial Bridge to relieve congestion.
